ei.title: 사후 정보 제시에서의 정보 생략과 기억 억제
ei.subject: 수능특강Light

fullPassage: A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to inhibit the retrieval of a particular piece of information by omitting it from a subsequent post-event presentation. Children appear to be particularly susceptible to this effect. Wright, Loftus and Hall presented children aged 9-10 years with a video depicting a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident), and then showed them the same video again some time later with a short scene added. The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second experiment, to create a story about it. Subsequent testing revealed that the children often failed to recall the omitted scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made better by their second viewing of the video, compared with controls who received no second viewing. Williams, Wright and Freeman found a similar effect when reference to a particular scene was omitted from a post-event interview. Their participants (a group of young children aged 5-6 years) were far more likely to forget a scene if it was omitted from the post- event interview.

questions.passage: A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to (A)[inhibit / enhance] the retrieval of a particular piece of information by omitting it from a subsequent post-event presentation. Children appear to be particularly susceptible to this effect. Wright, Loftus and Hall presented children aged 9-10 years with a video depicting a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident), and then showed them the same video again some time later with a short scene added. The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second experiment, to create a story about it. Subsequent testing (B)[revealed / concealed] that the children often failed to recall the omitted scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made better by their second viewing of the video, compared with controls who received no second viewing. Williams, Wright and Freeman found a (C)[similar / contradictory] effect when reference to a particular scene was omitted from a post-event interview. Their participants (a group of young children aged 5-6 years) were far more likely to forget a scene if it was omitted from the post- event interview.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② inhibit — revealed — similar: 정보 생략으로 기억 인출을 '억제'할 수 있고, 후속 테스트가 아이들이 생략된 장면을 회상하지 못했음을 '드러냈으며', 다른 연구에서도 '유사한' 효과 발견.

❌ ① enhance — revealed — similar: 기억 인출을 '향상'시키면 글 전체 논지(생략이 기억을 억제)와 모순.

❌ ③ inhibit — concealed — similar: '숨겼다'면 테스트 결과가 공개되지 않았다는 뜻으로 문맥 불일치.

❌ ④ inhibit — revealed — contradictory: '모순되는' 효과라면 두 번째 연구가 첫 번째와 반대 결과여야 하나, 실제로는 같은 결과.
det.tip: inhibit(억제하다) ↔ enhance(향상시키다). reveal(드러내다) ↔ conceal(숨기다). similar(유사한) ↔ contradictory(모순되는).

questions.passage: A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to inhibit the retrieval of a particular piece of information by (A)[omitting / including] it from a subsequent post-event presentation. Children appear to be particularly (B)[susceptible / resistant] to this effect. Wright, Loftus and Hall presented children aged 9-10 years with a video depicting a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident), and then showed them the same video again some time later with a short scene added. The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second experiment, to create a story about it. Subsequent testing revealed that the children often failed to (C)[recall / recognize] the omitted scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made better by their second viewing of the video, compared with controls who received no second viewing. Williams, Wright and Freeman found a similar effect when reference to a particular scene was omitted from a post-event interview. Their participants (a group of young children aged 5-6 years) were far more likely to forget a scene if it was omitted from the post- event interview.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① omitting — susceptible — recall: 사후 제시에서 '생략'하여 기억 억제, 아이들이 이 효과에 특히 '취약'하며, 생략된 장면을 '회상'하지 못함.

❌ ② including — susceptible — recall: '포함'시키면 기억 억제가 아니라 강화되어 논지와 모순.

❌ ③ omitting — resistant — recall: '저항력이 있다'면 아이들이 영향을 안 받는다는 뜻으로 원문과 반대.

❌ ④ omitting — susceptible — recognize: recognize(인식하다)도 가능하나, 원문은 recall(회상하다)이 정확한 표현.
det.tip: omit(생략하다) ↔ include(포함하다). susceptible(취약한) ↔ resistant(저항력 있는). recall(회상하다) vs recognize(인식하다).

questions.passage: A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to inhibit the (A)[retrieval / storage] of a particular piece of information by omitting it from a subsequent post-event presentation. Children appear to be particularly susceptible to this effect. Wright, Loftus and Hall presented children aged 9-10 years with a video (B)[depicting / distorting] a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident), and then showed them the same video again some time later with a short scene added. The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second experiment, to create a story about it. Subsequent testing revealed that the children often failed to recall the omitted scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made better by their second viewing of the video, compared with controls who received no second viewing. Williams, Wright and Freeman found a similar effect when reference to a (C)[particular / general] scene was omitted from a post-event interview. Their participants (a group of young children aged 5-6 years) were far more likely to forget a scene if it was omitted from the post- event interview.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ retrieval — depicting — particular: 정보의 '인출'을 억제하고, 일련의 사건을 '묘사하는' 비디오를 보여주며, '특정' 장면에 대한 언급이 생략됨.

❌ ① storage — depicting — particular: 정보 '저장'을 억제한다는 것은 원문 논지(인출 억제)와 다름. 정보는 이미 저장됨.

❌ ② retrieval — distorting — particular: 사건을 '왜곡하는' 비디오라면 실험 설계와 맞지 않음.

❌ ④ retrieval — depicting — general: '일반적인' 장면이라면 특정 장면 생략 실험의 핵심과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: retrieval(인출) ↔ storage(저장). depict(묘사하다) ↔ distort(왜곡하다). particular(특정한) ↔ general(일반적인).

questions.passage: A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to inhibit the retrieval of a particular piece of information by omitting it from a subsequent post-event presentation. Children appear to be particularly susceptible to this effect. Wright, Loftus and Hall presented children aged 9-10 years with a video depicting a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident), and then showed them the same video again some time later with a short scene ①<u>added</u>. The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second experiment, to create a story about it. Subsequent testing revealed that the children often failed to ②<u>recall</u> the omitted scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made better by their second viewing of the video, compared with controls who received no second viewing. Williams, Wright and Freeman found a similar effect when reference to a particular scene was ③<u>included</u> from a post-event interview. Their participants (a group of young children aged 5-6 years) were far more likely to ④<u>forget</u> a scene if it was omitted from the post- event interview.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① added: 짧은 장면이 '추가된' 비디오를 다시 보여줌 — 적절.

✅ ② recall: 생략된 장면을 '회상하다'에 실패함 — 적절.

❌ ③ included → omitted: 원문은 '특정 장면에 대한 언급이 사후 면담에서 생략(omitted)되었을 때'. 포함(included)되었다면 기억 억제 효과와 모순.

✅ ④ forget: 생략되면 장면을 '잊을' 가능성이 훨씬 높음 — 적절.
det.tip: omit(생략하다) ↔ include(포함하다). 정보를 생략해야 기억이 억제된다는 것이 글의 핵심.

questions.passage: A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to inhibit the retrieval of a particular piece of information by ①<u>omitting</u> it from a subsequent post-event presentation. Children appear to be particularly susceptible to this effect. Wright, Loftus and Hall presented children aged 9-10 years with a video ②<u>depicting</u> a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident), and then showed them the same video again some time later with a short scene added. The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second experiment, to create a story about it. Subsequent testing ③<u>revealed</u> that the children often failed to recall the omitted scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made ④<u>worse</u> by their second viewing of the video, compared with controls who received no second viewing. Williams, Wright and Freeman found a similar effect when reference to a particular scene was omitted from a post-event interview. Their participants (a group of young children aged 5-6 years) were far more likely to forget a scene if it was omitted from the post- event interview.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① omitting: 정보를 '생략함으로써' 기억 인출을 억제 — 적절.

✅ ② depicting: 일련의 사건을 '묘사하는' 비디오 — 적절.

✅ ③ revealed: 후속 테스트가 '드러냈다' — 적절.

❌ ④ worse → better: 원문은 '두 번째 시청으로 그 장면의 회상이 실제로 더 나아졌다(made better)'. 생략 없이 다시 보면 기억이 개선되므로, worse는 원문과 반대.
det.tip: better(더 나은) ↔ worse(더 나쁜). 두 번째 시청은 기억을 개선한다(통제군 대비).

questions.passage: A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to inhibit the retrieval of a particular piece of information by omitting it from a subsequent post-event presentation. Children appear to be particularly ①<u>susceptible</u> to this effect. The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second ②<u>experiment</u>, to create a story about it. Subsequent testing revealed that the children often failed to recall the ③<u>omitted</u> scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made better by their second viewing of the video, compared with ④<u>participants</u> who received no second viewing. Their participants (a group of young children aged 5-6 years) were far more likely to forget a scene if it was omitted from the post- event interview.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① susceptible: 아이들이 이 효과에 특히 '취약한' — 적절.

✅ ② experiment: '두 번째 실험'에서 이야기를 만들라고 함 — 적절.

✅ ③ omitted: '생략된' 장면을 회상하지 못함 — 적절.

❌ ④ participants → controls: 원문은 '두 번째 시청을 받지 않은 통제 집단(controls)과 비교'. participants(참가자)는 실험 참가자 전체를 가리켜 대조군 의미가 사라짐.
det.tip: controls(통제 집단) = 실험에서 처치를 받지 않는 비교 대상. participants(참가자) = 실험 참가자 전체.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② events: 일련의 '사건들'(음주운전 사건 등)을 묘사하는 비디오 — a series of events는 원문 표현.

❌ ① scenes: '장면들'도 가능해 보이지만 원문에서 a series of는 events와 결합하며, scenes는 비디오 내 개별 단위.

❌ ③ experiments: '실험들'은 비디오가 묘사하는 대상이 아님.

❌ ④ interviews: '면담들'은 사후 절차이지 비디오 내용이 아님.
det.tip: a series of events(일련의 사건들) — depict(묘사하다)의 목적어로 자연스러움.

det.analysis:
✅ ④ susceptible: 아이들이 이 효과에 특히 '취약한' — 실험 결과 아이들이 생략 효과에 잘 영향받음.

❌ ① immune: '면역의'는 영향을 받지 않는다는 뜻으로 원문과 반대.

❌ ② indifferent: '무관심한'은 효과에 대한 반응이 아닌 태도.

❌ ③ resistant: '저항력 있는'은 영향을 덜 받는다는 뜻으로 원문과 반대.
det.tip: susceptible to(~에 취약한) ↔ resistant to(~에 저항력 있는). be susceptible to = ~의 영향을 받기 쉬운.

det.analysis:
✅ ③ retrieval: 정보의 '인출'을 억제할 수 있다 — 기억에서 꺼내오는 과정(retrieval)이 방해됨.

❌ ① storage: '저장'은 기억 형성 단계. 이미 저장된 정보의 인출이 억제되는 것이 핵심.

❌ ② creation: '생성'은 정보 처리 개념이 아님.

❌ ④ transmission: '전달'은 정보를 다른 곳으로 보내는 것으로 기억 인출과 다름.
det.tip: retrieval(인출) — 기억에서 정보를 꺼내오는 과정. inhibit the retrieval = 인출을 억제하다.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>inhibit</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① suppress: '억누르다, 억제하다'로 inhibit과 동의어.

❌ ② promote: '촉진하다'는 inhibit의 반의어.

❌ ③ facilitate: '용이하게 하다'도 억제와 반대 의미.

❌ ④ accelerate: '가속하다'는 억제와 반대 방향.
det.tip: inhibit(억제하다) = suppress, restrain, hinder ↔ promote(촉진하다), facilitate(용이하게 하다).

det.analysis:
✅ ② following: '뒤따르는, 이후의'로 subsequent와 동의어.

❌ ① previous: '이전의'는 subsequent의 반의어.

❌ ③ simultaneous: '동시의'는 시간적 순서가 다름.

❌ ④ initial: '초기의, 최초의'는 subsequent와 반대 방향.
det.tip: subsequent(후속의) = following, ensuing, later ↔ previous(이전의), prior(사전의).

det.analysis:

det.analysis:
✅ ② general: '일반적인'은 particular(특정한)의 정확한 반의어.

❌ ① specific: '구체적인'은 particular의 동의어.

❌ ③ unique: '독특한'은 하나뿐이라는 뜻으로 반의어 아님.

❌ ④ detailed: '상세한'은 정보의 깊이에 관한 것으로 다른 축.
det.tip: particular(특정한) = specific, certain ↔ general(일반적인), universal(보편적인).

questions.passage: A number of recent studies have shown that it is possible to inhibit the retrieval of a particular piece of information by omitting it from a subsequent post-event presentation. Children appear to be particularly susceptible to this effect. Wright, Loftus and Hall presented children aged 9-10 years with a video depicting a series of events (such as a drink-driving incident), and then showed them the same video again some time later with a short scene added. The children were then asked to imagine the event or, in a second experiment, to create a story about it. <u>Subsequent</u> testing revealed that the children often failed to recall the omitted scene, and indeed their recall of that scene was actually made better by their second viewing of the video, compared with controls who received no second viewing. Williams, Wright and Freeman found a similar effect when reference to a particular scene was omitted from a post-event interview. Their participants (a group of young children aged 5-6 years) were far more likely to forget a scene if it was omitted from the post- event interview.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>Subsequent</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ preceding: '앞선, 이전의'는 Subsequent(후속의)의 정확한 반의어.

❌ ① consequent: '결과적인'은 시간적 순서가 아닌 인과 관계.

❌ ② eventual: '궁극적인'은 최종 결과에 관한 것으로 반의어 아님.

❌ ③ concurrent: '동시에 일어나는'은 시간적 동시성으로, 순서의 반대가 아님.
det.tip: subsequent(후속의) ↔ preceding(앞선), prior(사전의). subsequent = 시간상 뒤에 오는.

questions.passage:
(A) Wright, Loftus and Hall <u>presented</u> children aged 9-10 years with a video depicting a series of events.

(B) The student <u>presented</u> her research findings to the audience at the conference.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 presented가 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 제시하다, 보여주다 (실험 자극 제공) (B) 발표하다 (청중 앞에서 공개).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 제시하다, 보여주다 — (B) 발표하다: (A)에서 present A with B = A에게 B를 제시하다(실험 재료 제공). (B)에서 present A to B = B에게 A를 발표하다(공식적 발표).

❌ ① (A) 선물하다 — (B) 발표하다: '선물하다'는 물건 증여이지 실험 자극 제공이 아님.

❌ ② (A) 제시하다 — (B) 소개하다: '소개하다(introduce)'는 사람을 알려주는 것으로 연구 발표와 다름.

❌ ④ (A) 대표하다 — (B) 발표하다: represent(대표하다)와 present(제시하다)는 다른 단어.
det.tip: present A with B(A에게 B를 제시하다) vs present A to B(B에게 A를 발표하다). 같은 단어, 다른 구문과 의미.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"to leave out or exclude something, especially information or a detail"

det.analysis:
✅ ② omit: '생략하다, 빠뜨리다'로 영영풀이와 정확히 일치.

❌ ① inhibit: '억제하다'는 행동/과정을 막는 것이지 정보를 빠뜨리는 것이 아님.

❌ ③ depict: '묘사하다'는 빠뜨리기의 반대 방향.

❌ ④ recall: '회상하다'는 기억에서 꺼내오는 것으로 생략과 다름.
det.tip: omit(생략하다) = leave out, exclude, skip. to omit information = 정보를 빠뜨리다.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"easily affected or influenced by something, especially something negative"

det.analysis:
✅ ④ susceptible: '취약한, 영향받기 쉬운'으로 영영풀이와 정확히 일치.

❌ ① subsequent: '후속의'는 시간 순서에 관한 것.

❌ ② particular: '특정한'은 구체적 대상을 가리키는 것.

❌ ③ intensive: '집중적인'은 강도에 관한 것.
det.tip: susceptible(취약한) = vulnerable, prone. be susceptible to = ~에 취약한/걸리기 쉬운.

questions.passage: Subsequent testing _____(reveal) that the children often failed to recall the omitted scene.
questions.stem: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 과거 시제 문맥. Subsequent testing이 주어이고, 실험 결과를 서술하는 과거형 문장이므로 revealed가 적절.
det.tip: reveal(드러내다) → revealed(과거형). 실험 결과 서술은 과거 시제.

questions.passage: Children appear to be _____(particular) susceptible to this effect.
questions.stem: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 형용사 susceptible을 수식하는 부사가 필요. particular(형용사) → particularly(부사).
det.tip: particular(형용사: 특정한) → particularly(부사: 특히). 부사가 형용사를 수식.

questions.passage: Their participants were far more likely to forget a scene if it was _____(omit) from the post-event interview.
questions.stem: 다음 문장의 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 수동태 구문 'it was _____'에서 과거분사 필요. omit → omitted (자음 t 다음 -ed, t 이중자음).
det.tip: omit(생략하다) → omitted(과거분사). 1음절 + 단모음 + 단자음 → 자음 중복 + ed.
